key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast perovskite photoluminescence degradation over time, enabling early prediction of long-term stability from short accelerated-aging measurements.
engineering_relevance: This provides a faster, more explainable stability-screening tool for perovskite solar cell development, reducing the need for lengthy experimental aging tests.
method: Collected an experimental dataset of 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Featurized >86,000 PL spectra with a physics-informed model.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict PL intensity for unseen samples and compared it against baseline benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a diverse dataset of 167 materials and over 86,000 PL spectra, with the proposed model generalizing across material groups and outperforming baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the accelerated-aging dataset, so extrapolation to new chemistries or stress conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
